csv_project_name: AE for New Public Works Facility
csv_scope_of_work: The Consultant s role will be to complete a preliminary design of a new Public Works administrative and maintenance facility, providing space for Sewer & Drain, Highway and Vehicle Maintenance operations and including upgrades to the transfer station building and re-purposing of the existing site features for storage and to provide much-needed flood protection. Any new facility will need to be designed to mitigate flood risk. The study will include a space needs analysis, site analysis, existing building reuse/renovation recommendations (if practical), at least two preliminary conceptual design alternatives, and associated opinions of cost.
csv_disciplines_requested: Architecture Services, Interior Design/Space Planning, Civil Engineering, Surveying/GIS/Mapping, Inspection Services, Sanitation Engineering

title: AE for New Public Works Facility
short_description: Preliminary design for a new flood-resilient public works facility in Hampton, New Hampshire.
project_scope: Preliminary design study for a new public works administrative and maintenance facility serving Sewer & Drain, Highway, and Vehicle Maintenance operations. Scope includes upgrades to the transfer station building, reuse of existing site features for storage, flood protection measures, flood-risk-mitigating design, space needs analysis, site analysis, recommendations for reuse/renovation of existing buildings if practical, at least two conceptual design alternatives, and associated cost opinions.
services: Architecture services, interior design/space planning, civil engineering, surveying/GIS/mapping, inspection services, and sanitation engineering; preliminary design and conceptual alternatives.
relevance_explanation:
- Public works administrative and maintenance facility, not a bridge, stadium, long-span roof, or special structure.
- Early-stage design scope is positive, but the project appears to be a conventional municipal building.
- No indication of complex structural systems, large spans, lightweight design, or architecturally demanding features.
- Flood-resilience aspect is relevant but does not outweigh the otherwise low structural relevance for sbp.
- Includes architecture and civil/site planning rather than a clear structural engineering focus.
construction_cost_explanation: No construction budget is stated in the source. The documents mention only preliminary design, conceptual alternatives, and opinions of cost. Useful cost drivers: new administrative and maintenance facility, transfer station building upgrades, site reuse/storage, and flood protection measures.
fee_explanation: No fee information is provided in the source. The procurement is for preliminary design and related studies only; no explicit engineering fee or budget basis is stated.
references_qualifications: Consultant team requested in architecture, interior design/space planning, civil engineering, surveying/GIS/mapping, inspection services, and sanitation engineering. No specific minimum reference counts or qualification thresholds are stated in the source excerpt.
contracting_authority: Town of Hampton Municipal Offices, Hampton, New Hampshire, USA. Contact: Jennifer Hale. Phone: 603-926-6766. Fax: 603-926-6853. Email: jhale@hamptonnh.gov. Website: https://hamptonnh.gov/bids.aspx?bidID=106
notes: Mandatory pre-submittal meeting on 06/02/2026 at 10:30 AM EDT; RSVP to jhale@hamptonnh.gov. Solicitation documents available online. Project concerns a municipal public works facility with maintenance functions and flood protection/site resilience components.
